newsitem.title: USA: No need to raise U.S. interest rates -- lawmaker.
newsitem.headline: No need to raise U.S. interest rates -- lawmaker.

text.p: A fractional gain in May consumer prices confirms there is no worrsiome inflation to justify a hike in interest rates next month, the chairman of Congress' Joint Economic Committee said on Tuesday.

Committee Chairman Jim Saxton noted the Consumer Price Index barely advanced 0.1 percent in May, according to a Labor Department report on Tuesday, while the Producer Price Index published last Friday showed a 0.3 percent decline in wholesale prices last month.
"These prices data support the position that the Federal Reserve should not raise interest rates in the next FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting at the beginning of July," Saxton said.

He said that "forward-looking inflation indicators" monitored by the Joint Economic Committee, including commodity prices, bond yields and the value of the dollar, all confirm the lack of any inflation pressures.
"These price data show no evidence supporting Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes last March or in the near future," Saxton said.

The FOMC raised short-term rates a quarter percentage point on March 25. It kept rates steady at a subsequent May 20 meeting and is scheduled to meet again on July 1-2 to discuss interest-rate strategy.
